Official Synopsis

The Review (No Spoilers)

After watching countless movies and shows from the "modern" era, this film is a breath of fresh air. As far as I can tell, no niggers or jews were involved in its production -- that alone should tell you everything you need to know.

Surprisingly, on the IMDb cast page, Morgan Freeman is credited as a "Narrator." Don't let that fool you, I've reviewed the film's credits and confirmed it's false. Also, the entire film has zero narration. Indeed, it actually has very little dialogue.

The film is set during Europe's last Ice Age, 20,000 years ago. We follow the journey of Keda, the teenaged son of his tribe's Chieftain. In order to survive, the tribe must regularly hunt bison, all while braving hazardous lands full of predators. A sincere, good-hearted young man, Keda is gentle to a fault, but eager to follow in his father's footsteps, weak though his hunting and survival skills may be.

When a hunt goes tragically wrong, Keda becomes separated from his tribe. Alone, injured, short on resources and faced with a treacherous environment, Keda must do everything he can to survive the trek home... and become his own man along the way.

Contrary to what the trailers indicate, the entire film is set in "Soldean," a fictional language that took two years to create for the occasion. It is based on Proto-Nostratic, Proto-Eurasiatic and Proto-Dené–Caucasian languages.

The film's characters are believable, well-acted and sympathetic. With much of the film focusing on just two characters, monotony is avoided by featuring breathtaking shots (some real and others CGI) of expansive landscapes, sweeping horizons, starry skies and erupting volcanoes.

Perhaps the biggest treat of this film is that there's no kike propaganda, even though there could've easily been. There could've been a "muh climate change" message.
